20. What happens when an object's property values are changed after creation?
The object stores the latest assigned values in its fields. When an instance method accesses those fields, it uses their current values.
The new assignments replace the previous values. Therefore, the methods print Lobo, not Rucky.

23. How can a real-world problem be converted into an object-oriented Java program?
The problem can be converted into a Java program by following these steps:
Identify the real-world entities in the problem.
Identify what each entity has, such as name, age, or cost.
Identify what each entity does, such as eating, sleeping, or barking.
Define a class containing the corresponding fields and methods.
Create objects using the new keyword.
Store object references in variables when repeated access is required.
Assign field values and invoke methods through the reference variables.
This approach applies the concepts of classes, objects, properties,
, and references to represent real-world entities in Java.
